title: Tensor–Hom form of the exchange
statement:
Fix primes $p$ and $\ell\ne p$, an integer $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, a field $k_0$ with $q$ elements, and an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Choose an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside it with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, an integer $n\geq1$, and put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Assume a six-functor datum [def-sf-datum] on the bounded constructible finite-Tor coefficient categories $D^b_{ctf}(-,\Lambda)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], with its finite, completed integral, rationalized and common-stage coefficient conventions. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type $k$-morphism [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism], with $Rf^!$ the constructible exceptional inverse image
of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] (no admissibility datum is assumed;
every such $f$ is exceptionally admissible in the sense of
[def-trf-admissibility]), $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ and
$N\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$. Then there is a canonical isomorphism

$$
Rf_*R\mathcal H om_X(M,f^!N)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
R\mathcal H om_Y(Rf_!M,N),
$$

natural in $M$ and $N$ and compatible with finite reduction, scalar
extension, and shifts. ([fix-lem-tensor-adjunction]; the
proof is the one given there, recalled here because the whole formal core
rests on it.)

proof.text: Write $H(P,Q)=R\mathcal Hom(P,Q)$, $A_{M,N}=Rf_*H(M,f^!N)$ and $B_{M,N}=H(Rf_!M,N)$. Axiom (A1) of [def-sf-datum] supplies $f^!N$ and $Rf_!M$ in their finite-Tor domains. At $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ choose nonnegative dimension bounds $d_X,d_Y$ by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], using zero for an empty scheme. For $W=X,Y$, [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] gives a finite affine cover $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ by finitely generated $k$-algebras; [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components] makes the charts topologically Noetherian. A descending chain of closed sets in $W$ stabilizes: restrict it to each chart and take the maximum of the finitely many stabilization indices. Each open in $W$ is quasi-compact, since otherwise successively adjoining uncovered members of an open covering gives a strictly ascending chain of opens. Thus the affine open inclusions $j_i$ are quasi-compact.

source.place: Before Step 2: finite affine charts and dimension bounds; inherited step 1

proof.text: The inclusion $j_i:U_i\to W$ is finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type] and separated because its diagonal is an isomorphism. The affine $U_i$ is separated over $k$: its diagonal is induced by the surjection $B_i\otimes_k B_i\to B_i$. Its dimension is at most $d_W$ by [lem-weil-pbc-open-subspace-dimension-monotone]. Therefore [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude] restricts the two inputs with unchanged Tor intervals. Apply [cor-weil-finite-constructible-hom] on each $U_i$; [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] identifies its output with the actual restricted global internal Hom. For input intervals $[a,b]$ and $[c,e]$ these outputs are bounded constructible with the one common Tor interval $[c-b-2d_W,e-a+2d_W]$.

source.place: Before Step 2: separated-chart internal-Hom calculation; inherited step 1

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-finite-cover-ctf-locality] to each of the two global internal Homs, using the Noetherian finite affine cover and its single output interval established in steps 1–2. Its conclusion gives bounded constructibility and that same Tor bound globally, precisely the conditions of [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] and [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. No separatedness of $X$ or $Y$ over $k$ was required. Then [cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-proetale], applied to $H(M,f^!N)$ and the given separated finite-type $f$, puts $A_{M,N}$ in $D^b_{ctf}(Y,A_{E,n})$ too. The empty schemes give zero objects.

source.place: Before Step 2: finite-cover gluing of the two representing objects; second part of inherited split step 1

proof.text: At $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$, (A1) again supplies integral bounded constructible $f^!N$ and $Rf_!M$. Each of the two pairs defining $H$ has uniformly finite-Tor reductions by [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor]. [lem-coef-integral-hom-reduction] says that $H$ is derived complete and that its reductions are the finite internal Homs, preserving evaluation. Apply the finite affine-cover argument of steps 1–3 at each level, with the same input intervals and the same dimension bounds. The resulting constructible reductions have one common Tor and cohomology interval. Hence [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] puts both internal Homs in the integral bounded constructible category, and [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor] puts them in $D^b_{ctf}$. The unconditional ordinary adjunction in clause (1) of [fix-prop-adjunctions] is an adjunction between the integral bounded constructible categories; in particular its $Rf_*$ takes the first internal Hom to $D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$. Apply [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor] once more to obtain $A_{M,N}\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\mathcal O_E)$. This uses only the ordinary clause (1), not the conditional exceptional clause (2) of that node.

source.place: Before Step 2: integral domain check, with finite reductions and completed coefficient sheaves

proof.text: At $\Lambda=E$, [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] keeps the integral objects and replaces Hom groups by their tensor products with $E$. The operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], [def-weil-derived-direct-image], [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], and [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] on objects are their integral constructions, followed by this rationalization. Thus the two objects of step 4 remain objects of the rationalized category. At $\Lambda=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] represents $M,N$ and the finitely many operations involved over a common finite coefficient field; apply the preceding membership check there. By [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] the finite-Tor field categories are precisely these bounded constructible categories. Thus at every coefficient stage both $A_{M,N}$ and $B_{M,N}$ lie in the full category $\mathcal C_Y=D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$. The same definition identifies its Hom sets with the ambient Hom sets where an ambient realization is used.

source.place: Step 2: full finite-Tor category containing both represented objects at the field stages

proof.text:
Let $L$ range over $\mathcal C_Y$, exactly as in the current item proof. The tensor–internal-Hom adjunction is explicitly stated in [sk-def-sf-operations](i) for the derived operations at the coefficient stages of the datum. Together with (A1) and (A3) of [def-sf-datum], it gives natural bijections
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}_Y(L,B_{M,N})
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_!M\otimes^L L,N)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_!(M\otimes^L Lf^*L),N)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(M\otimes^L Lf^*L,f^!N)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(Lf^*L,H(M,f^!N))\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(L,A_{M,N}).
\end{aligned}$$
The second bijection is precomposition with $\operatorname{PF}_{f,M,L}^{-1}$, with precisely the type specified by axiom (A3) of [def-sf-datum]. The more restricted notation node def-sf-pf is not needed here; no separatedness of the structure morphisms of $X$ and $Y$ is imposed. Its invertibility is the required axiom (A3), applicable because both $M,L$ are finite-Tor bounded constructible. At finite coefficients [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude] and [lem-sf-tensor-ctf](ii) put $M\otimes^L Lf^*L$ in the finite-Tor category; at integral coefficients use [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible] and [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor], and at the field stages use their specified coefficient constructions. Thus the third bijection uses the constructible exceptional adjunction (A1) on its domain. The fifth uses the ordinary adjunction (A1); the first and fourth use tensor–Hom. Every integral tensor here is completed tensor. Naturality of the adjunction bijections and the projection transformation makes this chain natural in $L$, contravariant in $M$, and covariant in $N$.

source.place: Step 1: the five Hom bijections, inverse projection formula, and the precise domains of the exceptional adjunction

proof.text: Denote the composite bijection in step 6 by $h_L:\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_Y}(L,B_{M,N})\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_Y}(L,A_{M,N})$. Apply [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful] in the full category $\mathcal C_Y$, whose membership was established in steps 1–5. Explicitly set $a=h_B(1_B):B\to A$ and $b=h_A^{-1}(1_A):A\to B$. Naturality in $L$ gives $h_L(u)=a\circ u$ and $h_L^{-1}(v)=b\circ v$; applying the two inverse bijections shows $a\circ b=1_A$ and $b\circ a=1_B$. The required isomorphism has forward map $b:A\to B$. The bijection's naturality in $M,N$ implies the corresponding naturality equations for $b$ by the uniqueness in Yoneda. Since the finite-Tor category is full, this is also the claimed isomorphism in its ambient realization.

source.place: Tag 001P (categories-lemma-yoneda): fully faithful Yoneda on the full category containing both objects

proof.text: For finite quotient change define the global internal-Hom comparison as the transpose of scalar-extended evaluation. On the separated affine cover of steps 1–2 it is an isomorphism by [thm-coef-finite-hom]. The slice comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] identifies its restrictions with those affine comparisons; clause (1) of [lem-cbc-proetale-stalk-conservative] then makes it an isomorphism globally. Its evaluation equation holds globally by its defining transpose. For integral reduction, [lem-coef-integral-hom-reduction] already states the invertibility of that evaluation-defined comparison and preservation of tensor-Hom transposes. Thus both finite and integral reduction use the specified evaluation comparisons. Locality was used only to prove a morphism invertible, never to test equality of arbitrary derived morphisms.

source.place: Step 2: finite quotient and integral reduction comparisons; inherited coefficient step

proof.text: For integral scalar extension $E\subset L$, [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] gives a finite free map of completed ring sheaves $R\to S$ on either scheme, and identifies integral scalar extension of derived complete objects with ordinary $-\otimes_R^L S$. Apply [lem-sf-ringed-finite-free-hom-base-change] to the two internal-Hom inputs: its comparison is invertible and is the transpose of scalar-extended evaluation. The other integral operation comparisons are those of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension]. Their tensor/evaluation equation is precisely the balancing equation $(x\otimes a)\otimes(h\otimes b)\mapsto h(x)\otimes ab$, also at finite reductions. Hence the comparisons used in tensor-Hom transposition are the canonical evaluation-defined ones, independent of a free basis.

source.place: Step 2: integral scalar-extension internal Hom; finite-free argument extracted

proof.text: Let $T$ be a finite-reduction or scalar-extension functor at a stage where it is defined. Test the forward map $b$ of step 7 by a morphism $u:L\to A$: transpose under $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$, then tensor-Hom, then $Rf_!\dashv f^!$, precompose with $\operatorname{PF}_{f,M,L}$, and transpose tensor-Hom again. The result is $h_L^{-1}(u)$ for the bijection of step 6. Insert the comparisons of (A5) of [def-sf-datum] before and after these five operations. Its compatibility with the units and counits of (A1) and with the projection transformation (A3) makes the corresponding transposes equal; the tensor-Hom transposes commute by the evaluation identities established in steps 8–9 and the tensor-Hom adjunction of [sk-def-sf-operations]. Injectivity of transposition makes the two paths around the exchange comparison square equal. At rational coefficients these are the integral equations tensored with the field by [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. At algebraically closed coefficients use one common finite field for the finitely many objects and maps, and then their classes in the Hom colimit of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]; the scalar-extension cocycles make these classes independent of representatives. No reduction from field coefficients to a finite quotient is used.

source.place: Step 2: coefficient compatibility by the five transpositions; inherited coefficient step

proof.text: For shifts, use the signed internal-Hom comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]: $H(P[r],Q)=H(P,Q)[-r]$ and $H(P,Q[r])=H(P,Q)[r]$. Under these comparisons the chain for $(L,N[r])$ is the chain for $(L[-r],N)$; the right-adjoint shift comparisons are defined by transposing the shift comparisons of the left adjoints. To check the projection arrow rather than assume its shift compatibility, use its explicit construction [def-exchange-projection]: the proper projection map is the transpose of $(\varepsilon_p\otimes1)\circ\mu_p$, and the compact-support projection is its composite with $Rp_*(\gamma)$, where $\gamma$ is the open-extension tensor comparison and pullback composition. Shifting a tensor factor shifts this composite by the total-tensor convention, with $d_{C[r]}=(-1)^r d_C$; the tensor–Hom evaluation comparison uses the same signed convention. The two shifted transposition routes therefore agree. At integral coefficients the inverse-limit functor is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], so the same comparisons pass through the completed pullback and tensor constructions of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Rationalization and common finite stages have their induced shifts by the definitions cited in step 5. Consequently $h$ for shifted arguments is the shifted $h$, and the uniqueness in step 7 gives the shift square for $b$ in $N$, and in $M$ with the negative internal-Hom shift.

source.place: Step 2: shifts; signed evaluation and projection-transposition calculation

proof_origin.place: Steps 1–2, with independent domain checks and explicit comparison/shift calculations

blueprint_update.statement:
In the setting of [def-sf-datum], let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated
finite-type morphism, with $Rf^!$ the constructible exceptional inverse image
of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] (no admissibility datum is assumed;
every such $f$ is exceptionally admissible in the sense of
[def-trf-admissibility]), $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ and
$N\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$. Then there is a canonical isomorphism

$$
Rf_*R\mathcal H om_X(M,f^!N)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
R\mathcal H om_Y(Rf_!M,N),
$$

natural in $M$ and $N$ and compatible with finite reduction, scalar
extension, and shifts.

proof.text:
The adjunctions and the projection transformation used throughout are
those recorded in [fix-prop-adjunctions] and
[fix-lem-tensor-adjunction], in the form fixed by [def-sf-pf].
Step 1: for every $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ the adjunctions of axiom
(A1) and the tensor–internal-Hom adjunction of
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] give the chain

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}_Y\bigl(L,R\mathcal H om_Y(Rf_!M,N)\bigr)
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_!M\otimes^L_\Lambda L,N)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y\bigl(Rf_!(M\otimes^L_\Lambda Lf^*L),N\bigr)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X\bigl(M\otimes^L_\Lambda Lf^*L,f^!N\bigr)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X\bigl(Lf^*L,R\mathcal H om_X(M,f^!N)\bigr)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y\bigl(L,Rf_*R\mathcal H om_X(M,f^!N)\bigr),
\end{aligned}
$$

the second isomorphism being the *inverse* of the projection formula
(axiom (A3), [def-sf-pf]), the third the adjunction
$Rf_!\dashv Rf^!$, and the first, fourth and fifth the tensor–internal-Hom
adjunction together with $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$. Step 2: the chain is natural
in $L$, so the two objects represent the same functor on
$D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$; the Yoneda lemma applied to degree-zero morphisms
of that triangulated category gives the canonical isomorphism, whose
naturality and compatibilities are those of the ingredients.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q98-7e40c49ee (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read all of it: the item, all 11 steps, both new nodes, all 34 cited statements, the main-20261015 statement and proof, the unit record and the duplicate candidates. The statement is unchanged and agrees with main-20261015; no target is weakened. The coefficient category is pro-etale D^b_ctf at every stage, f^! is the constructible exceptional inverse image, and no admissibility is assumed. It is not a target, so no base-change morphism applies, and no SGA source is cited. Step checks: (1–2) cor-weil-finite-constructible-hom needs separated X and is applied on separated affine charts. The input intervals come unchanged through lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude, and the output [c-b-2d,e-a+2d] is uniform because d_W is the same on every chart. (3) The locality node's hypotheses are exactly what steps 1–2 establish. cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-proetale needs only f separated. (4) Uniform reduction bounds come from residue-tor and lem-coef-integral-hom-reduction; only clause (1) of fix-prop-adjunctions is used. (6) PF^-1 has the A3 direction and every bijection stays inside its ctf domain. (7) Yoneda gives the map A->B in the stated direction. (8–10) The evaluation-defined comparisons and A5 give the coefficient compatibility. (11) The sign conventions for shifts are consistent. Both new nodes are true and tested on small cases. Locality: empty cover, a single member, and gluing the strata Z∩(X minus earlier charts) in a Noetherian space. Finite-free Hom: S=R, d=0, P=0 or Q=0, and the Hom_S(P⊗S,-)=Hom_R(P,-) plus finite-sum argument. Neither restates a clause of the item. Neither duplicates an existing node: lem-coef-integral-finite-extension covers only D^b_c on separated X; det-thm-(int-)restriction-glue use condensed conventions at O_E/E/Qlbar; lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension does not specify the evaluation transpose. I accept the declared tool uses. Two B3 fixes, both in fixes/: (a) lem-sf-finite-cover-ctf-locality now cites def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves, def-weil-constructible-subset and def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf; (b) lem-sf-ringed-finite-free-hom-base-change now cites def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves and def-pc-kflat-complex for the derived tensor, and lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction and lem-pur-rhom-global-sections for the adjunction that defines transposes. Neither fix changes a meaning or creates a cycle. Minor points, accepted: LeanSearch was rate-limited and is recorded as unavailable; the step-8 slice compatibility with evaluation is a one-line termwise check.; 2 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
